verifications.claim: President Donald Trump fired U.S. Attorney General Pam Bondi on April 2, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Trump fires Attorney General Pam Bondi (https://www.cnbc.com/2026/04/02/...)' ; R3: 'Trump replaces US Attorney General Pam Bondi published at 20:39 BST 2 April' ; R7: 'President Trump fired Attorney General Pam Bondi on Thursday' (article dated 2026/04/02)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly confirm Trump fired Bondi as AG on April 2, 2026, with matching dates in URLs and publication times.

verifications.claim: Pam Bondi served a 14-month tenure as U.S. Attorney General.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R7: 'Bondi’s firing ends a turbulent 14-month term atop the Justice Department' ; R8: 'Attorney General Pam Bondi will be leaving after just 14 months'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly state her tenure was 14 months, consistent with start in Feb 2025 to April 2026.

verifications.claim: A BBC report details that Pam Bondi's firing was largely driven by President Donald Trump's frustration regarding her handling of the Epstein files and a perceived lack of prosecutions against his political opponents.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'The president's frustration had been growing with her leadership at the justice department - particularly over her handling of the Epstein files... Trump has often demanded unrestricted control of the justice department to pursue investigations into targets of his choosing, even when he was warned there was no evidence to do so' ; 'the president reportedly grew frustrated with her handling of the Epstein files, as well as the Justice Department’s unsuccessful efforts to prosecute several of the president’s high-profile political opponents'
verifications.reasoning: BBC (R3) directly attributes firing to Trump's frustration over Epstein files handling and lack of prosecutions of opponents.

verifications.claim: CNN reports that Bondi served the shortest tenure for a confirmed attorney general in 60 years.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R5: 'she wound up serving the shortest tenure for a confirmed attorney general in 60 years'
verifications.reasoning: CNN article (R5) exactly matches the claim phrasing.

verifications.claim: Sources reported in CNN and The Guardian mention that Pam Bondi's inability to manage the fallout from the Epstein files, which allegedly harmed Trump, was a major factor in her removal.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2 (Guardian): 'Trump reportedly fired her in part... over the way she handled the Epstein files' ; 'Trump’s frustration over how Bondi handled the Epstein files illustrates how the matter continues to haunt his administration' ; R5 (CNN): 'The most damaging aspect of Bondi’s tenure was undoubtedly the Epstein files' ; R9 (CNN): 'Trump had been frustrated with Bondi... including her handling of the Jeffrey Epstein files'
verifications.reasoning: Both CNN and Guardian sources cite Epstein files mishandling as a key frustration and factor in firing, implying harm to Trump/administration reputation.

verifications.claim: According to CNBC, Pam Bondi was expected to be replaced by Deputy Attorney General Todd Blanche.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'our Deputy Attorney General... Todd Blanche, will step in to serve as Acting Attorney General' ; Bondi: 'transition the office of Attorney General to the amazing Todd Blanche'
verifications.reasoning: CNBC (R1) directly reports Trump stating Blanche will replace Bondi as Acting AG, matching the claim.
